source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
finding: Sample many chain-of-thought paths and take the most frequent final answer. It beats greedy chain of thought on every arithmetic and commonsense set tested.
numbers: PaLM-540B GSM8K 56.5 to 74.4 (+17.9); SVAMP 79.0 to 86.6 (+7.6); AQuA 35.8 to 48.3 (+12.5). code-davinci-002 GSM8K 60.1 to 78.0 (+17.9), SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2. Up to 40 paths (Table 2).
limits: Gain shrinks near ceiling (PaLM AddSub +1.8). Needs a short extractable final answer.
agent_relevance: Core of S3 plus code-side S7: many independent draws, code counts the answers.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-Consistency, scale results
finding: The gain depends on model size. Small models gain little.
numbers: GSM8K: UL2-20B 4.1 to 7.3 (+3.2); LaMDA-137B 17.1 to 27.7 (+10.6); PaLM-540B +17.9. Across arithmetic sets: +3 to +6 for UL2-20B, +9 to +23 for LaMDA-137B.
quote: The gain is relatively lower for smaller models
limits: Voting only works when the right answer is the most common one.
agent_relevance: Gate voting by class and base accuracy (G12).

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-Consistency vs sample-and-rank and sampling settings
finding: Counting answers beats ranking samples by the model log-probability at equal sample count. The gain holds across temperature, top-k and nucleus settings.
numbers: GPT-3 code-davinci-001: sample-and-rank gain much smaller than vote gain (Fig 3). PaLM-540B GSM8K robust over T 0.3 to 0.7, top-k 20/40, top-p 0.9/0.95 (Fig 4).
limits: Model likelihood is a weak selector; answer agreement is stronger.
agent_relevance: Do not let the model score its own samples. Code counts answers.

source: Wang et al. (2022) Self-Consistency, agreement as confidence; imperfect prompts
finding: The share of samples agreeing with the final answer tracks accuracy, so low agreement signals doubt. Voting also repairs flawed few-shot prompts.
numbers: LaMDA-137B imperfect prompt: greedy 17.1 to 14.9, vote recovers the loss. Zero-shot CoT plus vote +26.2 (Table 8). Agreement strongly correlated with accuracy on GSM8K (Fig 5).
limits: Agreement is an uncertainty estimate, not proof of truth.
agent_relevance: Use disagreement among attempts as the code trigger for S5/S6 (G1: doubt only on a signal).

source: Cobbe et al. (2021) Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems (GSM8K)
finding: Earlier route: sample many solutions, pick the one a trained verifier ranks highest. Introduced GSM8K (7.5K train, 1K test).
numbers: Verifier gives about the same boost as a 30x larger model compared with finetuning; verifiers scale better with data (authors claim).
quote: verifiers scale significantly better with increased data
limits: Needs verifier training data; voting needs none.
agent_relevance: Voting is the training-free cousin of this. Our S7 prefers code checks, then votes.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
finding: Coverage (any sample correct) grows log-linearly over four orders of magnitude of samples. With a real verifier this turns into accuracy.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% with 1 sample to 56% with 250, above the 43% single-sample state of the art. CodeContests, Gemma-2B: 0.02% to 7.1% at 10,000 samples.
limits: Only converts to accuracy where an automatic verifier exists (tests, proof checker).
agent_relevance: Where S4 can run a check, many draws then code selects is strongly supported.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys, voting plateau without a verifier
finding: With no automatic verifier, majority vote and reward-model selection stop improving near 100 samples while coverage keeps rising.
numbers: Llama-3-8B-Instruct MATH: coverage 82.9% at 100 samples to 98.44% at 10,000; majority vote or reward model only 40.50% to 41.41%. Gap widens with samples (Fig 7).
quote: the occurrence of rare, correct solutions does not affect the most common answer
limits: Boundary: the vote cannot find a rare correct answer.
agent_relevance: Keep vote size small. More votes do not rescue hard items with no check.

source: Li et al. (2024) More Agents Is All You Need (Agent Forest)
finding: Plain sampling and voting improves with more instances and stacks on top of CoT, debate and other methods.
numbers: Gains: GSM8K +12 to +24 points; MATH +6 to +10; Chess +1 to +4; MMLU +5 to +11; HumanEval +4 to +9. Llama2-13B with ensemble 59% on GSM8K beat Llama2-70B at 54%.
limits: Gain larger for harder tasks (MATH 34-200% relative vs GSM8K 16-69%) and smaller models (28-200% vs 8-16% for GPT-3.5). Some debate combinations failed.
agent_relevance: Cheap model, many votes can beat one bigger model sample. Voting is orthogonal to other scaffold steps.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Are More LM Calls All You Need? Towards Scaling Laws of Compound Inference Systems
finding: Majority vote can get worse as calls increase. Easy queries improve, hard queries (where the plurality answer is wrong) get worse.
numbers: Tasks: MMLU Physics, TruthfulQA, GPQA, AVeriTeC. MMLU Physics split: Vote easy 53% / difficult 47%; Filter-Vote 56% / 44%. A model fitted on few samples predicts the best number of calls.
quote: performance on easy queries and lower on hard queries
limits: Direct failure case: when the correct answer is not the plurality, more samples harden the wrong one.
agent_relevance: Cap N. Spend extra effort on hard items through other operators rather than more votes.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Universal Self-Consistency for LLM Generation
finding: Ask the model to pick the most consistent among N free-form answers, so voting works without exact-match answers.
numbers: GSM8K gpt-3.5-turbo: greedy 73.4, SC 78.5, USC 77.8; MATH 33.2 / 38.0 / 38.1. PaLM 2-L GSM8K 85.7 / 90.4 / 90.2; MATH 30.8 / 37.9 / 37.4. TruthfulQA GPT-judge 62.1 to 67.7 (one model). BIRD-SQL about equal to execution voting.
limits: USC on GSM8K fell with 16 samples; gains stop after 5 on SummScreen; response order effect minor (std 0.1-0.3). Needs long context.
agent_relevance: Selecting among open-ended outputs by model-chosen consensus works about as well as code voting, but the selector is a model call (G5, G8 caution on judges).

source: Aggarwal et al. (2023) Let us Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency
finding: Stop sampling once a clear majority has formed. Spends samples where answers disagree.
numbers: 17 reasoning and code datasets, 3 LLMs: sample budget cut up to 7.9x, typical 2 to 4x, average accuracy drop under 0.1%.
limits: Stopping rule assumes the majority is right; shares the vote failure on hard items.
agent_relevance: Sample 2 then 3 and stop on agreement: matches G11/G12 and the 2-to-4 attempts in S3.

source: Li et al. (2024) Escape Sky-high Cost: Early-stopping Self-Consistency (ESC)
finding: Sample in small windows and stop when a window is unanimous. Large savings with comparable accuracy.
numbers: Average samples cut: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%, Last Letters -67.4%.
limits: Saving smallest on the hardest set (MATH). Needs a window size w and cap L.
agent_relevance: Easy items stop early; hard ones keep sampling. Fits spending by difficulty (G12).

source: Taubenfeld et al. (2025) Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs (CISC)
finding: Weight each vote by the model confidence in that path. Same accuracy with fewer paths.
numbers: Nine models, four datasets: CISC beats plain SC in nearly all settings and cuts required paths by over 40% on average. Gemma2-9B MATH: 8 CISC samples beat 30 SC samples.
quote: Surprisingly, the most calibrated confidence method is actually the least useful for CISC
limits: Confidence must be judged within a question, not across questions.
agent_relevance: Weighted votes are an option, but G10 says reasoning text is not evidence; use only if confidence is measured, not narrated.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Soft Self-Consistency Improves Language Model Agents
finding: Exact-match voting fails when actions are many and distinct (agent tasks). Scoring candidates by likelihood (soft) works better there.
numbers: CodeLlama-34B: Soft-SC beats SC by 6.6% absolute on WebShop and 4.2% on average at k=10 over four agent datasets; up to 4% with GPT-4 on WebShop. Gain on Bash 8.8% as size rises 7B to 70B.
quote: majority voting fails to provide consistent gains on such tasks
limits: Boundary: open action spaces make vote ties; the method needs token probabilities.
agent_relevance: In an agent loop, vote on the final answer, not on each step action. Per-step voting gets few repeats.

source: Wang & Zhou (2024) Chain-of-Thought Reasoning without Prompting (CoT-decoding)
finding: Branch on top-k first tokens; CoT paths already exist in the model, and answer confidence picks them. Beats voting without a CoT prompt.
numbers: GSM8K without prompts: Mistral-7B greedy 9.9%, SC (10 paths) 12.9%, CoT-decoding 25.1%. PaLM-2 L greedy 34.8%, CoT-decoding 63.2%.
limits: Authors note the most common answer can be wrong while a minority path is right, which defeats the vote in that setting.
agent_relevance: Counting answers is not always the right selector; the right path can be a minority. Harvest candidates (S4) before voting.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via RL
finding: Voting still helps a long-reasoning model, and helps a non-reasoning model far less.
numbers: AIME 2024: DeepSeek-R1 pass@1 79.8% to cons@64 86.7%. GPT-4o 9.3 to 13.4 with 64 votes; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 16.0 to 26.7. Distill-Qwen-7B 55.5 to 83.3; Distill-Qwen-1.5B 28.9 to 52.7.
quote: majority voting across 16 samples per problem yields minimal improvement in GPT-4o
limits: Reasoning models cost far more tokens per sample; voting multiplies that.
agent_relevance: Voting complements a reasoning pass. Keep it to few attempts (G11).

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: Best use of extra compute depends on question difficulty. Best-of-N with a verifier is the baseline that search and revision beat.
numbers: Compute-optimal strategy beat best-of-N using about 4x less compute. A smaller model with test-time compute can beat a 14x larger model (FLOPs-matched) on easy and intermediate questions.
quote: with the most challenging questions, we observe very little benefits
limits: Hardest questions gain little. Verifier needed.
agent_relevance: Supports G12: allocate by difficulty. Easy: few samples. Hard: do not just add samples.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Inference Scaling Laws: Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
finding: Compares greedy, majority vote, best-of-N, weighted vote and tree search across model sizes and budgets on GSM8K and MATH.
numbers: Weighted majority vote error falls then converges as samples grow; small models are compute-optimal at low budgets (Fig 1). Llemma-7B with tree search beats Llemma-34B on MATH across all strategies tested.
limits: Voting saturates; search scales further.
agent_relevance: Vote has a ceiling; draws past saturation are wasted.

source: Stroebl, Kapoor, Narayanan (2024) Inference Scaling fLaws: Limits of LLM Resampling with Imperfect Verifiers
finding: Resampling until a verifier passes is capped when the verifier gives false positives. False-positive rate rises as single-sample accuracy falls.
numbers: On HumanEval and MBPP (limited test coverage), optimal number of attempts is often under 10; the curve bends down as false positives are accepted.
limits: A weak check cannot be outrun by more draws.
agent_relevance: Our S4/S7 must test on the unfitted part (G3); a weak check makes extra draws harmful.

source: Smit et al. (2024) Should we be going MAD? Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
finding: Debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling of multiple reasoning paths on multiple-choice QA.
numbers: Benchmarked debate against Medprompt and self-consistency across domains; debate not reliably better. Tuned debate settings (Multi-Persona) did better, read by authors as hyperparameter sensitivity.
quote: do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies
limits: Result depends on tuning; cost and time also compared.
agent_relevance: Supports G9 (no debate): independent votes are the cheaper baseline.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models
finding: Repeated samples from one model are very alike, and different models are alike too. Samples are not independent draws.
numbers: Over 26K open-ended queries: average pairwise similarity of same-prompt responses typically exceeds 0.8 at top-p 0.9, T=1.0; for one model in 79% of cases it exceeds 0.8.
quote: even under maximally aggressive sampling, LMs still fail to generate diverse responses
limits: Open-ended queries, not math. Votes there reward the mode, not good ideas.
agent_relevance: Samples correlate, so effective vote size is below N; use fresh contexts and varied prompts (S3), and do not vote in open mode.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Universal Self-Consistency, code generation
finding: Without running code, model-chosen consensus matches voting on execution results.
numbers: gpt-3.5-turbo: ARCADE greedy 26.0, SC-Exec (strict) 29.8, SC-Exec (fuzzy) 30.3, USC 30.1; BIRD-SQL execution accuracy greedy 42.4, SC-Exec 45.6, USC 45.5.
limits: Execution voting still needs a runnable environment. USC cost is one long-context model call.
agent_relevance: When code can run, execute and group by behaviour (S7). A consensus pick is the fallback when it cannot.

source: Li et al. (2024) More Agents Is All You Need, stacking with other methods
finding: Sampling and voting adds to other prompting methods rather than replacing them.
numbers: Llama2-13B GSM8K: CoT 0.39 to 0.56 (+0.17) with ensemble; SPP 0.19 to 0.42 (+0.23). MATH CoT 0.04 to 0.06.
limits: Gain depends on task difficulty; failed cases when combined with debate for Llama2 models.
agent_relevance: A cheap vote layer can sit on top of the scaffold; test each combination, it may fail.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1, voting on distilled small models
finding: Large voting gains on AIME for small distilled reasoning models, where single-sample accuracy is high but unstable.
numbers: AIME 2024 pass@1 to cons@64: Distill-Qwen-7B 55.5 to 83.3; Distill-Qwen-14B 69.7 to 80.0; Distill-Qwen-32B 72.6 to 83.3; Distill-Llama-8B 50.4 to 80.0.
limits: AIME has only 30 problems, so each gain rests on few items; 64 samples of long traces are costly. Not independently replicated here.
agent_relevance: On a small test set with long traces, a 64-way vote can add 10 to 30 points; at our budget (G11) expect far less.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Universal Self-Consistency, sample count limits
finding: More candidates stop helping, and may hurt, because the selecting model has to read all of them.
numbers: GSM8K accuracy fell at 16 samples; SummScreen no gain beyond 5; TruthfulQA and BIRD-SQL kept improving. Authors name about 8 samples as the sweet spot.
limits: Context length and model counting error cap the selector; code counting does not have this limit.
agent_relevance: Let code count answers. A model should not tally many long candidates (G5, G8).
